COMPLIANCE / DATA & DESIGN

Our approach to project data, authorship and handoff, plus a plain-language account of how this website works.

OUR PROJECT APPROACHDESIGN, DATA & ACCOUNTABILITY
Project data ↘Rights & tools ↘Website privacy ↘

Privacy starts
with the brief.

For work involving personal data, agree the purpose, data needed, access, suppliers and retention with the client before processing starts. Use anonymised or sample data for design whenever possible.

  1. Map the data. Establish who controls it, why it is needed, and which systems receive it.
  2. Reduce collection. Design forms around necessary fields and clear choices.
  3. Agree safeguards. Document access, deletion and any processor or transfer arrangements with the client’s responsible team.
  4. Review the experience. Check privacy information, consent choices and user controls before handoff.

GDPR responsibilities depend on the project and each party’s role. The project agreement records them; this page is not a certification or a guarantee of legal compliance.

EDPB guidance on privacy by design ↗

Clear ownership.
Clear tool choices.

Agree deliverables, source files and usage rights before making the work. Record third-party font, image, audio and software licences, with costs approved separately.

Any proposed use of AI tools should be disclosed, with the client’s approval before sharing confidential material. Client data should not be uploaded to a public AI tool without an agreed basis and safeguards.

Final work is reviewed for relevance, accuracy and rights. A shared review log records decisions, feedback and scope changes.

THIS WEBSITE / LAST UPDATED 12 OCTOBER 2026

What this site
does with data.

Tracking
The site code uses no analytics, advertising trackers or tracking cookies. Fonts and animation libraries are served with the site.
Project form
Name, email and brief stay in page memory. No form data is submitted to a website server. The form prepares a mailto draft; you choose whether to send it through your email app.
Copying
“Copy inquiry text” writes your draft to your clipboard only when you press the button.
Email
Messages you send go to theredstudio@gmail.com, hosted by Google. The studio uses your message to respond and discuss the project. For access or deletion requests, email the same address.
Hosting
The public site runs on GitHub Pages; private previews run on OpenAI Sites. Hosting and sign-in providers may process connection, security and account data under their own policies. See GitHub’s privacy statement ↗ and OpenAI’s privacy policy ↗.

We do not ask for financial records, IDs or other sensitive documents in this form. Arrange a suitable channel before sharing confidential project materials.
